item.title: Team masseur to start World Championships men's road race as Slovakia's only rider after desperate situation
item.author: James Moultrie
item.content:encoded: Alongside the superstars Remco Evenepoel, Mathieu van der Poel and Isaac del Toro on the start line of the World Championships men's elite road race on Sunday will be a surprising entry: Vladimír Kováčik, a masseur for the Slovakian national team.It's been a decade since Slovakian superstar Peter Sagan won the second of his three world titles in a row, and while still not one of the major cycling nations, the situation hasn't turned that bleak since the all-time great's retirement. Slovakia has more than enough talent to be able to field a strong team between the likes of Lukáš Kubiš (Unibet Rose Rockets), Martin Svrček (Soudal Quick-Step) and Matthias Schwarzbacher (EF Education-EasyPost), but a series of events led them to this being the only solution.Their ranking meant they were due to be fielding a four-man team, but between injuries and rider schedules taking priority, they found themselves in an emergency, and a potentially costly one, as not fielding a team could see their national championships drop into the B category for 2027, with a cut to the number of UCI points on offer.Late cancellations left them unable to nominate a replacement, with the window for registration closing on September 11, so they were forced to turn to a member of the support staff to protect the future prospects of Slovakian riders."The only nominated racer [for the women's race], Nora Jenčušová, had to end the season prematurely due to injuries and adverse health conditions. Likewise, the only relevant nominated men - Lukáš Kubiš, Matthias Schwarzbacher and Martin Svrček had to cancel their participation at the last moment," read a post from the Slovakian federation's Instagram."Due to the late cancellation of their participation, it was no longer possible to supplement the nomination adequately. Given the UCI rules and the fact that the World Championships are taking place in Canada, the situation was only possible to be resolved through a member of the Slovak team, who was already on site and met the conditions of the start. At the same time, it is not possible to further include U23 in the elite category of quality racers, because they could lose the opportunity to start in their age category."A 28-year-old masseur for the national team, Kováčik has raced previously, but according to his ProCyclingStats profile, not since 2017. That season he was 32nd in the national time trial championships in Slovakia, and he had raced at Paris-Roubaix juniors the season before that – though he did not finish.In the women's elite road race, they will similarly be fielding only one rider, but the situation hasn't been quite as desperate, with Tereza Kurnická taking the start as Jenčušová's replacement, a multiple-time Slovakian national champion in mountain biking.National coach Jakub Vančo explained the consequences in greater detail, stating how essential the points could be for their goal of qualifying for the 2028 LA Olympics, but made sure to stress that the masseur's entry was nothing more than a "formal representation"."For the national champion, the drop is half, for the second one almost two-thirds. We would count the losses in the hundreds. These points are equal to winning a World Tour stage race, which is beyond our capabilities," Vančo told "So we have to fulfil our obligation to the UCI to have someone compete in the elite races. Moreover, next year will be a qualifying year for the 2028 Olympics."Our participation will only be formal. We will have representation in the form of a person who is here and formally meets the conditions and licenses." Slovakia has performed well throughout the ongoing championships in Montreal, Canada, with top young talent and Visma-Lease a Bike rider Viktória Chladoňová winning the women's under-23 road race and Richard Riška taking eighth in the equivalent men's race. It's the future of these riders and the rest of their developing talent that the decision has been made for."Minimum representation of Slovakia in the Elite category is important in terms of maintaining the ranking and point positions required for future nominations for the World Championships, European Championships and Olympic Games," read the post on the federation's Instagram. "Although such a solution is not ideal and it is not a decision that we would accept easily, in the current situation it is necessary to preserve start possibilities for prospective Slovak cyclists and cyclists, such as Chladoňová, Kubiš, Schwarzbacher, Ungerová, Svrček, Riška, Novák, Andacká and other quality juniors. We therefore believe in understanding this extraordinary situation.""I would like to thank Terka Kurnická and Vlad Kováčik for starting in the elite category. With their participation, we will not lose important points that will be useful to us in the future," said Chladoňová.Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: 2027 combined UCI World Championships to include 20 disciplines, including Gravel, with demanding road circuit in Sallanches
item.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: As the UCI Road World Championships in Montreal, Canada prepare to reach their crescendo with the elite women's and men's road races, the organisers of the next Worlds presented a hugely ambitious project for a combined championships bigger than any in history.Bringing together all of the UCI's disciplines except for cyclo-cross and snow bike, the Haute Savoie combined UCI World Championships will include 20 disciplines from BMX to Trials - bringing in the Gravel World Championships for the first time - and gather some 15,000 athletes from 207 nations to compete for 288 titles.The road races will take place in Sallanches, the site of the 1964 Road World Championships where Eddy Merckx won his first title as an amateur at age 19, and where Bernard Hinault won his world title in 1980. Each race will take place fully on a 13.3km circuit that includes 185m of climbing on the Côte de Domancy, a 2.5 km climb that has an average gradient of 9.4%.There will be no lengthy run-out for the elite riders, just 20 laps of the circuit for an incredibly demanding 265 kilometres with 5,700 metres of climbing for elite men, 12 laps/158.6km and 3,420 metres for elite women and under-23 men, 9 laps for under-23 women and junior men and six laps for junior women.Even the time trials will have a climb. The elite and under-23 time trials are 37.2km with a start and finish in Annecy, encircling Lac d'Annecy and climbing over the Côte de Talloires - a 1.5km climb at 6.5% average - for a total of 265 metres of climbing, while juniors begin in Doussard at the south end of the lake for 20.3km and 202 metres of climbing. In the mixed relay, the men will cover the flat first 16.9km while the women will tackle the climb and 20.3km, making for some interesting tactical decisions.But the championships will be much, much bigger than just road cycling, with three BMX events, Indoor Cycling, Esports, Cycle Speedway (think short-track speed skating on bikes), Gran Fondo, Gravel, five Mountain Bike events (Cross-country, Marathon, Downhill, Enduro and E-Enduro), bike Polo, Pump Track, Para-cycling Road, Track (Junior, Elite, Para) and Trials.The combined event is the brainchild of David Lappartient, who said he originally had the idea to combine the five Olympic disciplines every four years while campaigning to become UCI President. During Friday's presentation of the 2027 Worlds, he explained, "Once [I was] elected ... we said to ourselves: 'Why limit ourselves to five? Why not include our various competitions of the year?'"The journey led to the 2023 Glasgow World Championships with 13 disciplines and, after a chance meeting while on holiday in Châtel that led to Lappartient presenting the awards of a Gran Fondo, he met the president of the province, Martial Saddier."That was the first meeting," Lappartient recalled. "And he said, 'I have a dream. I want to bring back the UCI Road World Championship in Sallanches, where Bernard Hinault won. When can it be?'. I said, 'Look, 2025 is in Africa, 2026 could probably be Montreal - here we are - and in 2027, we set up the combined World Championships, but 2028 is free.""But he said, 'Yes, but we are elected until March 2028 ... Why not 2027, the combined?' [I said], 'It's all the disciplines, you know, it will be like 20 UCI World Championships together.' And he said, "OK, done. I'll take that."The agreement held and one year from now, the 'Cycling Games' will be spread across the province, with Les Gets, a long-time MTB World Cup host, hosting the mountain bike cross-country and downhill. Only track cycling will be outside Haute Savoie. Rather than use the nearby Grenoble velodrome, track cycling events will be held in the Saint-Quentin-en-Yvelines National Velodrome outside of Paris.Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Norris demands ban for Colapinto after Azerbaijan GP crash
item.content:encoded: Reigning world champion Lando Norris thinks Franco Colapinto deserves "at least a one-race ban" for causing a pile-up at Formula 1's Azerbaijan Grand Prix.On a lap 36 restart in the streets of Baku, Colapinto locked up his cold front tyres and aimlessly speared into Alpine team-mate Gasly into Turn 1, with Norris also collected by the tangling pair.The incident knocked both Gasly and ...Keep reading

item.title: Norris wants F1 race ban for Colapinto
item.author: Valentin Khorounzhiy
item.content:encoded: Lando Norris says Franco Colapinto should face a Formula 1 race ban for his error during the Azerbaijan Grand Prix that took Norris, Colapinto and Pierre Gasly out of the race.After a fairly processional first 30-plus laps of the Baku race, Colapinto had a massive lock-up while entering Turn 1 on a safety car restart while running in 10th place, seemingly caught out by the rate of deceleration from the Mercedes of Kimi Antonelli ahead of him.He avoided hitting Antonelli but instead had to hug the inside wall and never scrubbed off anywhere near enough speed, ploughing into Alpine team-mate Gasly in the braking zone, with the chain reaction also eliminating Norris.It was an error that Norris, who had had a particularly difficult weekend up to then and had his own Turn 1 mistake just before the safety car, did not take kindly to.Norris stressed that he had not seen the replay at the time of speaking but said: "I think the FIA should be more strict and start handing out bans for this kind of stuff. It's just careless from people."It costs a lot of money, all my parts are in the bin now. People should just get banned, because that's not driving that deserves to be in Formula 1."On whether race leader George Russell's approach to the restart bunched up the field too much, he said: "George can do what he wants."In Formula 1 I think you expect drivers to anticipate things, know grip is going to be low, know tyre temps are low - they weren't even that low."In Formula 1 you want to be against the best drivers in the world, and when stuff like this happens, it's because...yeah, [it] shouldn't be there."He reiterated later that he wanted "at least a one-race ban" for this kind of crash.A race ban in F1 requires a driver to amass 12 penalty points in a 12-month period - which has become a lot less likely since the FIA revised its approach to penalty points, seeking only to penalise what it perceived as actively dangerous driving or unsportsmanlike conduct.By virtue of a number of yellow flag infringements, Colapinto is joint-top with Carlos Sainz in the current penalty points leaderboard - but, pending a verdict on this incident, that still means only four points, so there is no precedent under the current system by which he would be banned for the next round.Colapinto, for his part, was immediately apologetic on the radio and maintained that tone in his media appearance."I was out of control completely. Not a lot more to say than sorry to the team, to Pierre, of course, to all the factory," he said."I'm sorry to Lando also. I'm sorry to everyone. It was a big mistake, of course."He didn't respond specifically to Norris's suggestion of a race ban but said: "I do expect to get something [in terms of a penalty], of course. I don't know, I'm not a steward."A 10-second penalty was assessed against Colapinto as the Baku race concluded - but as he did not reach the finish, this is now set to be converted to a grid drop.

item.title: Russell wins despite late Verstappen challenge
item.content:encoded: Mercedes' George Russell holds off a late challenge from Red Bull's Max Verstappen to win an Azerbaijan Grand Prix enlivened by two late safety car periods.

item.title: Russell denies Verstappen in Azerbaijan GP punctuated by two safety cars
item.author: Jack Benyon
item.content:encoded: George Russell ended a barren run without a Formula 1 victory in the Azerbaijan Grand Prix by just 0.196s over Max Verstappen, with championship leader Kimi Antonelli recovering to fifth from 16th in part thanks to a pair of safety cars for crashes.Russell did everything a leader on a street circuit with a long straight on it should do: he got a good start, immediately cleared the one-second overtake window, and had extended his lead to 12 seconds by the time of the first pit stops.His biggest early cause for concern was "nibbling" the wall at the exit of Turn 15 on lap 25 of 51, but he otherwise ran untroubled until Alex Albon crashing at Turn 4 on lap 31 erased his advantage.The safety car benefitted Russell's team-mate Kimi Antonelli most.Championship leader Antonelli started 16th and actually lost a spot at the start, then took 17 laps to pass seven cars and make it to the points-paying positions. While his progress wasn't as rapid as his comeback win at Monza from 19th, it was risk-averse and steadier with the championship lead likely in mind.He caught and passed Franco Colapinto after erasing a just under four-second gap for ninth and then was gifted eighth when Lando Norris's disappointing race continued as the McLaren driver went straight on with a lock-up at Turn 1.At the point of the safety car Antonelli was eighth and 35s off Russell, but the safety car bunched the field to give him a better chance of progressing and allowed him to switch to the favoured soft tyre.He immediately made up a place on the restart as a massive melee broke out at Turn 1.A massive, near-comical lock-up from Colapinto smashed him into Alpine team-mate Pierre Gasly - who'd been seventh on the restart - and also took Norris out, while Liam Lawson was also spun in the concertina effect behind by Arvid Lindblad. "I love getting taken out by my team-mate," said a sarcastic Lawson, while Alpine lost a double-points finish in the chaos - much to Gasly's displeasure and Colapinto's apologies.In the highest-pressure scenario of having Verstappen behind, Russell absolutely nailed the restart on lap 39 but Verstappen remained in overtake mode range until three laps later, and then Verstappen set the fastest lap of the race to close back in - refusing to accept defeat.All the way until two laps to go Verstappen stayed within range and subjected Russell to pressure, until Russell finally built a 1.4s gap, but then Verstappen closed back in on the run to finish line on the final lap once both had cleared the scene of Valtteri Bottas's crashed Cadillac.But Russell was just able to hold on for his first win since the Austria GP in late-June."After the double-yellow I had no boost, had no power," said Russell after the race.Verstappen charged through the field from his eighth-place starting spot in the early stages, and despite some bickering between himself and his engineer over the mediums, and intense early pressure from Isack Hadjar, drove a fine race to take second. He'd passed Oscar Piastri for second already after the first safety car restart.Hadjar bagged an amazing result to take third after three races out injured, and was clearly faster in the early stages and played a great team-mate race by offering to stay behind Verstappen.Fourth-place finisher Charles Leclerc was passed by both the Red Bulls and appeared to struggle for pace, making a podium unlikely on the day, and it could have been worse had Piastri hadn't taken himself out of the battle with a lock-up at the first corner that sent him into the runoff area, compounding McLaren's disappointing day.Antonelli received damage to his floor after being clipped by Ollie Bearman on the first safety car restart, and initially struggled to clear Lewis Hamilton, but finally got past five laps after the second restart at Turn 1 and went no further, taking fifth in another comeback drive.Hamilton was the only driver in the top 10 other than Russell to finish where he started, perhaps reflecting Ferrari's race pace struggles.Behind him, the Alpine-induced crash created chaos and brought a host of cars well out of points contention into play.In-the-news Esteban Ocon may be losing his Haas seat but vaulted team-mate Bearman between the two safety cars, but then was bested on the last lap by just 0.030s - with Lindblad stealing the spot at the line. He avoided a penalty for the Lawson incident and made some opportunistic overtakes to make the best of a tough weekend with seventh place.Ocon took eighth ahead of Bearman, while the upgraded Williams bagged a point through Carlos Sainz, who was as low as 19th after his early stop.Hulkenberg missed out on the point with 11th, ahead of Lawson, Gabriel Bortoleto, Piastri and Sergio Perez.

item.title: Racing defensively not an option for bullish Remco Evenepoel and Wout van Aert in World Championships road race, but it's up to Seixas and France 'to make it a long and tough race'
item.author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
item.content:encoded: "What mistake will I find hard to forgive myself for if I didn't become world champion on Sunday? That I raced defensively," Remco Evenepoel told in a press conference held at their national team's residence at the Hôtel Mortagne on Friday evening.Evenepoel and Van Aert are just two of several favourites heading into the elite men's 273.7km that includes 3,800m of elevation gain across 12 laps of the Mount Royal circuit and the Camillien-Houde climb (2.3km at 6.2%).Only the strongest riders will survive this race of attrition, with noted rivals including Paul Seixas (France), Mathieu van der Poel (Netherlands), Tom Pidcock (Great Britain) and Isaac del Toro (Mexico), who won on this circuit just two weeks ago at the Grand Prix de Montreal.Evenepoel secured his fourth elite time trial world title last weekend and arrived in Montreal having taken victories at the Clasica San Sebastian and Grand Prix de Quebec; he was also second overall at the Tour de France this year behind five-time winner Tadej Pogačar (Slovenia).Pogačar will not line up to defend his world title won in Kigali last year, after crashing heavily at the Vuelta a España, and Evenepoel doesn't believe that it is Belgium's responsibility to make the race difficult."It is not up to us to do that. Wout van Aert and I are two finishers. Someone like Paul Seixas has to come in alone. Everyone knows that. So the French will have to make it a long and tough race," he said in a interview. "I don't need to be afraid to go to the finish with a group."Even so, Evenepoel said that racing defensively would be his biggest regret.He last won the elite men's road race world title in 2022 in Wollongong, while Van Aert's long list of accomplishments has yet to yield a rainbow jersey on the road.Van Aert comes into this weekend as a favourite after a successful Vuelta a España, where he won two stages, posted eight top-10s, and took the points classification jersey. His biggest win this year, and one of the most memorable, came at Paris-Roubaix, where he hoisted the cobblestone trophy above his head for the first time in his career.A rainbow jersey to match would be a fitting ending to a season of firsts for Van Aert. He reminded the press that he finished second at the Grand Prix de Montreal in 2022 and will understand the circuit's demands. "I don't need to convince anyone, except myself, that this course suits me," he told .Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Yankees Rivalry Roundup: AL West madness reaches new low
item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: Having moved a scheduled Saturday game against the Orioles up to Friday for a straight doubleheader, the Yankees and O’s split the twin bill. Baltimore blew out Brendan Beck and company in a 10-2 loss in the opener—an ignominious follow-up to CC Sabathia’s number retirement—but Ryan Yarbrough and Will Warren combined to lead them to 17 strikeouts in the 6-3 nightcap win. Most importantly, everyone remained healthy. Wins and losses don’t matter for the regular season at this point! Now, they wait at home for the storm to pass today and see if they can play a Game 162 tomorrow. If not … see you on Tuesday for the Wild Card Series, Boston.Here’s what else was going on Friday among the remaining AL playoff hopefuls.Tampa Bay Rays (97-63) 2, Philadelphia Phillies (87-73) 0We’ll only take a minute on this one since—with all due respect to the playoff hopes of our friends in Philly (but boy is it suddenly getting tense with the Diamondbacks hot on the trail)—it really doesn’t mean much with Tampa Bay locked into the top AL seed. The Phils got a really nice outing from ace Cristopher Sánchez, who fanned 10 Rays in seven innings of work. But he did allow an RBI single to Jonny DeLuca in the first and a solo shot to catcher Nick Fortes in the second, and with the Phillies absolutely sputtering … yeah, that was it. Freddy Peralta blanked Philly through 5.1 before a quartet of relievers completed the four-hit shutout, Bryan Baker notching his 41st save of the season.Boston Red Sox (86-74) 4, Chicago Cubs (88-72) 3 [Game 1]It took a little longer than anyone expected, but the Red Sox officially locked themselves into the No. 5 seed in the American League and a date with the Yankees in the Wild Card Series. The best-of-three will begin on Tuesday with all games in the Bronx. At first, it seemed like Boston’s odd skid would continue when the Cubbies plated three within the first four outs. Tyrone Taylor had doubled in Seiya Suzuki following a one-out walk in the first, and the trio of Matt Shaw, Michael Busch, and No. 9 hitter Miguel Amaya continued the mini-parade against Alec Gamboa in the second with with a single and a pair of doubles, Amaya’s going off the Green Monster to drive in a pair.Part of that rally had involved Shaw getting thrown out on a grounder to third though, and Chicago never scored that fourth run. They would rue that result, with typical starter Jake Bennett getting his first relief appearance in anticipation of the Wild Card showdown and throwing 3.2 scoreless. Greg Weissert and Raymond Burgos continued to keep the Cubs off the board for the rest of the game as their offense rallied off Clay Holmes. A rare error by Dansby Swanson brought in the first Boston run in the fourth, and Holmes allowed a leadoff single to former Yankees teammate Isiah Kiner-Falefa in the fifth, followed by a Roman Anthony double. He got one more out, but Caleb Thielbar entered and allowed a game-tying knock from Adley Rutschman.The Red Sox took the lead in the seventh, breaking the tie off Aaron Civale when Anthony tripled and Connor Wong doubled him in. With Weissert and Burgos silencing Chicago, that was all she wrote. The only downside for Boston was that surprise story Mickey Gasper had to leave the game early with biceps discomfort.Boston Red Sox (87-74) 2, Chicago Cubs (88-73) 0 [Game 2]The weather got gloomier as the day went along but the Red Sox left Fenway with a clean doubleheader sweep. Boston kept Brayan Bello in playoff tune-up mode despite coming off an outing of eight innings of 11-K, one-run ball, and they still twirled a shutout. Bello blanked Chicago through four, departed with his pitch count at 58, and gave way to rookie Jedixson Paez, making his fifth career appearance. Paez outpitched Bello, fanning five in five shutout frames to earn his first career win.David Peterson’s own five zeroes for the Cubs were in vain. The scoreless tie was broken up in the eighth with IKF and Jahmai Jones (another former Yankee) on base after walks. Wilyer Abreu cracked a double off Ryan Rolison to plate both runners. That was all Boston needed. The Cubs had hoped to host a Wild Card Series at Wrigley, but that’s looking unlikely now with the Padres a game and a half ahead of them. Game 162 will determine their flight path, and they’ll need a flight just to play it. The nor’easter is not supposed to get any better in Beantown over the weekend, so the Sunday game will be at a neutral site: Tropicana Field. Let’s get weird.Texas Rangers (79-81) 2, Minnesota Twins (76-84) 10When Jacob deGrom was rehabbing from Tommy John surgery, opportunities like this one undoubtedly drove him. Yes, the AL West is lousy, but the Rangers can easily win it and they had deGrom out there against a team playing out the string in the Twins. Even with Joe Ryan on the bump opposing him, they felt great. Instead, Minnesota clobbered deGrom and tallied six in the second, Luke Keaschall delivering the big blow on a two-run triple. The two-time Cy Young Award winner was tagged for eight runs in four innings of work. The news got worse for the Rangers learned that top bat Josh Jung broke his hand on a hit-by-pitch; he’s likely done for 2026. This one had to hurt, and deGrom was furious at himself in the postgame, saying multiple times that he was “embarrassed.”Houston Astros (79-81) 5, The Athletics (64-96) 6Well don’t worry Jacob because remember: the AL West is lousy. The Rangers lost while the Astros were still playing on Friday, so they had a golden opportunity to seize control of the AL West, especially because they own the tiebreaker and were facing a terrible A’s team. Said terrible A’s team held off Houston and won, 6-5. A six-run sixth proved to be enough for the A’s offense as Hunter Brown’s once-solid outing went by the wayside with awful relief from Bennett Sousa, who failed to record a single out and allowed three runs. Henry Bolte smacked a two-run triple in the frame and the A’s had a commanding 6-1 lead. Houston did fight back, in part because the A’s bullpen is horrific. Cam Smith homered and a rally in the eighth broke the score to 6-5 with runners on second and third after a wild pitch. Baby Bomber alum Luis Medina fanned Smith though and Houston was held at bay. Nelson Velázquez got a one-out walk in the ninth to put the go-ahead run on against Hogan Harris, only to be erased on a Jeremy Peña double play ball, stranding Yordan Alvarez in the on-deck circle. For the first time in MLB history, we are guaranteed a full-season division winner with either a .500 record or worse because neither Houston nor Texas can be better than 81-81.Cleveland Guardians (84-76) 12, Kansas City Royals (68-92) 9Funky one in KC. The Guardians maintained their hot streak and withstood rallies from the Royals to win late without actually getting all that many hits. They had a dozen runs scored but only nine hits. Carter Jensen slugged two homers and drove in five for the Royals, but it wasn’t nearly enough, even with a tied-up ballgame at 7-7. walks and a fielder’s choice in the eighth led to Cleveland plating three without a hit before the surging Angel Martinez drove in two with a double to make it a 12-7 game. Salvador Perez’s 324th career homer cut into the lead in the ninth, but the Guardians held on to maintain their one-game lead in the AL Central.Chicago White Sox (83-77) 6, Colorado Rockies (57-103) 1Munetaka Murakami clobbered a pair of dingers to reach 35 in his rookie MLB season, and both came off countryman Tomoyuki Sugano, who he’d homered against twice in NPB play. Sean Burke threw 5.1 innings with one run allowed, and all that was easily plenty for the Pale Hose to take care of business on the South Side. They’ll just need some help from KC if they’re going to pass Cleveland for the division again.

item.title: Road World Championships 2026 elite women's road race LIVE - The battle for the rainbow jersey begins in Montreal
item.author: Lyne Lamoureux

Welcome to our live report on for the elite women's road race on the final weekend of the 2026 UCI World Road Championships in Montréal, Canada.September 26, 2026 – 8:37 AMReigning champion Magdeleine Vallieres of Canada shared her thoughts on social media on the eve of the road race.September 26, 2026 – 8:42 AMWill Dutch racer Demi Vollering finally win a world title today? She lines up as the top favourite, having swept almost all before her this season.September 26, 2026 – 8:52 AMMore on Vollering from Laurens ten Dam, the Dutch team coach: "She is incredibly focused, that's true. Two days after the Tour de France, I got the first message already from her, 'OK, job's not finished'. I was like, 'OK, she's on'," Ten Dam told on Thursday evening.'Job's not finished' – Demi Vollering keeping quiet on game plan as she leads Dutch squad at Road World ChampionshipsTwo-time Tour de France Femmes winner thrives on responsibility this year as lone team leader for first rainbow rewardSeptember 26, 2026 – 8:55 AMAlong with Vallieres, Belgian leader Lotte Kopecky is the only previous World Champion lining up at the start. She won twice before, in Glasgow in 2023 and Zurich in 2024.Speaking on Friday, Kopecky acknowledged that Demi Vollering stands out as the favourite, but said plenty of other contenders are in the mix.'She might well be the woman to beat' – Lotte Kopecky acknowledges Demi Vollering is top World Championships favourite but points to strong field of contenders'If that top day comes, then a lot is possible' says two-time world champion of her own chances in MontrealSeptember 26, 2026 – 8:58 AMThree minutes until the start in Brossard - more on the route coming up.It is sunny in Brossard, with cool temperatures around 12°C, but the day should warm up, as the forecast calls for a high of 23°C in Montréal.September 26, 2026 – 8:59 AMThe 140 riders representing 57 nations, including new countries of Panama, the Philippines and Saudi Arabia are off.They will face 2570 metres of elevation gain over the 180.4km course featuring the closing Mount Royal circuit.September 26, 2026 – 9:08 AMStarting on the South Shore in Brossard, the women head south on an approximately 43km loop through Carignan, Chambly, and Richelieu in the Montérégie region before returning to Brossard and heading to Montréal.The peloton will then ride the Samuel-De Champlain Bridge towards the Mount Royal circuit which the women will tackle eight times, after having 73km in the legs already. The now-iconic circuit features several major challenges: the Voie Camillien-Houde, the Chemin de la Polytechnique, and the tough false flat rising along Avenue du Parc to the line.September 26, 2026 – 9:10 AMThe flag drops, and the race is on after a 4km neutral section. Peloton is spread across the road with the Dutch team massed at the front.September 26, 2026 – 9:13 AMMischael Alhazmi from Saudi Arabia is the first attacker but is quickly back in the peloton.September 26, 2026 – 9:19 AMLots of chatter in the peloton as they roll by fans on the side of the road.September 26, 2026 – 9:22 AMCanada's Maggie Coles-Lyster and Alison Jackson are at the front and in the middle of the peloton, controlling things for now for their teammate, defending champion Vallieres Mill.September 26, 2026 – 9:33 AMGreece’s Argyro Milaki and Israel’s Rotem Gafinovitz attack out of a right-hand turn and get a small gap with 166km to go.Six riders try to come across to the head of the race.September 26, 2026 – 9:34 AMOne of the riders trying to come across to the duo was Canada's Alison Jackson, and the move is nullified. September 26, 2026 – 9:36 AMAnother attack by Gafinovitz with Antri Christoforou (Cyprus) jumps on, but once again, the move is shut down. Portugal's Beatriz Rosso counters solo, and there is no immediate reaction from the pelotonSeptember 26, 2026 – 9:41 AMMore riders jump from the peloton and make it across the 15-second gap to Rosso. The move includes Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), and Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria)September 26, 2026 – 9:44 AMTallest rider in the peloton, Teniel Campbell (Trinidad & Tobago) attacks to bridge across and that gets an immediate reaction from Alison Jackson. Jackson seems to be trying to get into a break and the peloton, led by the Dutch team, shuts that down immediately.September 26, 2026 – 9:47 AMCampbell is not giving up, as she attacks once again, and more riders jump on her wheel. But the peloton doesn't want more riders to join the four riders in the break and Campbell can't escape.September 26, 2026 – 9:49 AMFour riders made it into the break, initiated by Beatriz Rosso (Portugal) with 162 km to go, and she was joined by Natalie Quinn (USA), Marte Berg Edseth (Norway), and Gergana Stoyanova (Bulgaria). The quartet have 44 seconds with 154km to go. September 26, 2026 – 9:54 AMAnother rider tries to jump to the break but the Dutch team reels her back in. They don't want to let any other rider to join the move.September 26, 2026 – 9:59 AMThe Dutch team is lined up at the front of the peloton, with some wind impacting the riders, controlling the gap, now up 1:40 to the break.

item.title: A new twist for 30th year of Tour de Langkawi with trio of summit finishes that will have sprinters fighting to 'just survive'
item.author: simone.giuliani@futurenet.com (Simone Giuliani)
item.content:encoded: A win is never all there is at stake in any race, but somehow at Le Tour de Langkawi it's a fact that doesn't quietly tap away in the background but leaps into the spotlight with a deafening roar. For a start, the long-running Malaysian event offers a rare chance to launch a career, while for others it is a last chance to save it for those riders yet to secure a contract for 2027. Then there are the crucial points at stake in the never-ending relegation battle, and its current position near the end of the season also often makes it a farewell tour for riders who have decided, or had decided for them, that it is time to step away from the sport. Altogether, it delivers the ingredients for a heady and emotion-filled, no-holds-barred battle with the backdrop of an exotic location plus a hot and humid climate which will have the riders raising a sweat even just walking to sign in at the start of each of the eight stages from September 27 to October 4. The race, which pulls together teams from the WorldTour, ProTour, Continental ranks and national teams for a race in a region which prizes its high-level UCI race opportunities, given they are limited, will also be throwing some new elements into the mix for its 30th edition this year.Usually the sprinters are in focus for much of the event, with a decisive climbing day in the mix that is often decisive in the General Classification battle, but this year there are three summit finishes to add fire to the overall fight, with organisers pointing to the race as among the toughest editions ever. It's a welcome move for the riders who enjoy the uphill, but the sprinters and others who may not be pure climbers but perhaps thought they may be able to hang in there for one day and have a shot at the GC. "Yeah, the organisers have done a good job of removing any hope for riders like myself of having any chance at the GC with how hard they've made it this year," quipped Aaron Gate (XDS-Astana), the winner of the final stage of last year's race.Sprinter Fernando Gaviria (Caja Rural-Seguros RGA)was even more succinct when asked what he thought about the trio of climbing days: "For me it's just survive."These will be days when the fast men become allies in the autobus, looking to beat the time limit rather than enemies, getting through so they can battle once again. Those among the key sprint contenders include last year's three-time winner Matteo Malucelli (XDS-Astana) – although we are yet to see if there may be any impact in stage from a training crash on Saturday that saw him quickly subbed out of the pre-race media conference line-up as his teammate Gate was subbed in. The potential sprint competition includes the five-time Giro d'Italia and two-time Tour de France stage winner Gaviria along with Modern Adventure's Riley Pickrell, though the Canadian rider is unfortunately one teammate down even before the race has even begun. Leo Hayter posted on social media that while he made the journey to Malaysia, he then discovered that he had pericarditis, so he has had to end his season. There is only one flat stage for the sprinters – from Shah Alam to Kampar – before the climbing begins, with the introduction of the new ascent of Gunung Jerai as a shorter but steep finale for stage 2. Stage 3 then delivers an early category 2 challenge, which could well be a break launching point, though it flattens to give the fast-finishers another potential chance in Kuala Kangsar.But the next two stages, with their long and challenging ascents to the finish line, are unquestionably all about the climbers. These include new revelation speed-skater turned cyclist Jasch Lennart (Tudor), Jan Castellon (Caja Rural-Seguros RGA), Nicolas Breuillard (Total Energies), Harold Martín López (XDS-Astana) and Jonathan Caicedo (Wheeltop Rotor Chengdu), who won the 2.Pro ranked Tour of Magnificent Qinghai in July.When the Ecuadorian champion, who in 2020 won a Giro stage on top of Mount Etna, was asked if he considered himself the favourite, Caicedo said, "My goal is a top ten finish in the race. I was training very hard in Ecuador; I think I'm good for the race, I'm ready for this."Stage 4 heads into the Cameron Highlands – where overall race winner Simon Carr claimed victory in 2023 – with the road steadily ascending for more than 40km to the line. Then there is a second stage in a row that is finishing with a Hors-category climb, as the race on stage finishes in the Genting Highlands, which is an ascent that crowned Max Poole as the winner in 2024.From there, stage 6 from Pandan Indah to Rembau offers some early category 3 challenges but flattens out after the first 20km, while stage 7 from the vibrant historical location of Melaka to Batu Pahat has nothing in the way of obstacles for the sprinters but the final stage to Putrajaya delivers a category 3 climb 50km from the line which could prove a launching point for an attack as the very last chance at a tour filled with riders looking for them unfolds.Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. Subscribers get unlimited access to exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go!

item.title: 'A top three would be a hole-in-one' - McNulty, Simmons and Jorgenson give USA the best chance in decades for World Championships road race
item.author: laura.weislo@futurenet.com (Laura Weislo)
item.content:encoded: The last American rider to win on the same course in the Grand Prix de Montreal, Brandon McNulty, sees the 2026 Worlds as his country's best shot at their first elite men's title since 1993."It's the best team I think the U.S. have had," McNulty told after the time trial on Sunday. "Of course there's going to be crazy good guys from all the nations, so we have our work cut out. I think we have a good team to race super aggressively and try to do something.There's a ton of strong guys that we still don't think have ever really beaten before. So it's gonna be hard, but we have numbers to at least play our cards well."The US team have McNulty, Matteo Jorgenson and Quinn Simmons as their protected riders. After Neilson Powless withdrew from the team due to illness, according to USA Cycling, he has been replaced by Riley Sheehan, who had felt snubbed by being named as a reserve. The team also has Kevin Vermaerke, Artem Shmidt, Larry Warbasse, and Sean Quinn. McNulty, third in the GP de Montreal two weeks ago with Simmons, who finished fourth just behind, are the top contenders, together with Jorgenson, who was second overall in Tirreno-Adriatico this year, and remains one of the country's top one-day race competitors. caught up with Team USA's sports director for the elite men's race, Mike Creed, who seemed realistic about the team's chances based on the superstars they're up against - even in the absence of Tadej Pogačar, who is out because of his crash in the Vuelta a España. Isaac del Toro (Mexico), Remco Evenepoel and Wout van Aert (Belgium), and Paul Seixas (France) will be hard for the US riders to beat."[A top five] might be the best we can do, depending on who's in front," Creed tells . "We're more capable of getting a medal with multiple guys at this race than ever. That doesn't mean we should, or it'll be a failure if we don't."Matteo [Jorgenson] was there and thereabouts at Québec [eighth -ed.] and he's going to have to have better legs on the day. I'm not writing him out, but he's acknowledged that. Kevin [Vermaerke] came out of the Vuelta - he spent like the last 10 days in the breakaway, so like if he's a little cooked, it wouldn't be the most surprising thing in the world. So, if you figure that we have two guys who don't have question marks over them about their form. [It will be] clear we made a mistake if we don't have anyone in the first 15," he added before giving a golf metaphor. "Par is top 15, top 10 is like a birdie, and I think top five, top three is a hole-in-one."Obviously, it's a World [Championships], and you want to dream for the sky, but the fact is just because we are excited to be in North America and have a really good team doesn't mean that Wout and Remco aren't who they are. I love the idea of a Rocky movie triumph - I'll be the happiest guy in the world if that happens, but I don't want these guys to make moves based off of a cinematic background score."Creed was able to watch the Under-23 Women and Junior Men's races to see how the races played out on the quite arduous Montreal circuit - 13.4 kilometres long with two significant climbs and very little flat roads in between."It was similar to how I thought it was going to play out, not because I'm incredibly smart or anything, but just because the course runs a certain way. In the women's race, when [the breakaway] had two minutes, you're like, 'They're not really making any inroads,' and then when the bigger-name riders went, they got it down to 30 seconds really, really quickly," says Creed."Then, [it was the] same thing in the Junior Men's race. Unless it's a bigger group than three or four - it has to probably be like six or seven - for it to be that dangerous. Otherwise, it's just really hard to be out there by yourself or in a small group, with the fast downhills where the pack can really pick up a lot of speed - free speed, accelerating out of the turns. All these things that just really add up when you're solo or in a small group."There's no room for error - you can't get caught behind; you don't want to chase. It's not like Remco [Evenepoel] in Montreal, where he bridged to the leading five or six by himself. Even as strong as he is, he got there, then on the next lap [he paid for it]. So it's not a climb that you want to do a lot by yourself unless everyone else is already smoked."You saw in the Women's Under-23 race, the Australian girl [Felicity Wilson-Haffenden], she just was dropping bombs on people. And even then, she went just a little too early, and it kind of gassed her."In the Junior Men's race, Spain's Benjamín Noval attacked out of the bunch with 45km to go, reached the breakaway, then dropped them to go solo for almost two laps. It's the kind of scenario that a time trial world champion like Noval can pull off - and one Evenepoel can realistically do, too. How can the US team keep that from happening?"By making sure that the guys are as fresh for that attack as possible," Creed replies. "You can't make Remco not Remco. You can only just prepare yourself the best you can for that move, and then hope for a little bit of luck after that. It's not always fun to have that in a race plan; you want as little 'hope' as possible in a race plan. But ultimately, I think there's probably two other guys that eight times out of ten can follow Remco from bottom to top."That would be Seixas and Del Toro."Even then, they've got to have a fairly decent race leading into it. I think McNulty, six or seven times out of 10, is going to be able to stay with that, especially if he has a clean race. Simmons about the same, Matteo more or less the same. Because there is a drafting section in the middle of the climb. It's steeper at the bottom, then you can draft in that main part, so..."Although the team had not yet held their strategy meeting at the time of our conversation, Creed says the riders were all "on the same page and really open to playing the cards close to their chest"."I think we really want the best possible result. We all do."In order to get their best shot at a world title, Creed says the race has to be as hard as possible before the end of the 110-kilometre run-in from Brossard."I think McNulty and Quinn and Matteo are very durable riders, and the more time on the pedals for everyone, the better. It could be windy at the start and there are some open sections. I don't think it would be something where you'd get Qatar-style echelons - it won't split to like 30 [riders] and then keep it all the way to the line. But it could just cause some being on the pedals and a little bit more stress than most people would generally like for a 270km race."The run-in to the circuits is not exactly straightforward. It's got a good little bump in it; it could be crosswinds over the bridge... I might be tempting fate saying that, because maybe we'll end up on the bad side of something, but I think as much of a shit-fight of a race as possible suits us. It eliminates a lot of variables."Along with Belgium, Creed says the French team, who are fully behind Seixas, will be dictating the race."I would be surprised if France made the climb easy once," he says. "I'm sure France wants as many hard climbing kilometres as humanly possible. They probably don't want Wout to go up the road, and then have them chasing while Remco sits on. That's probably not a very enviable position. Belgium is very blessed in having a Remco because he can go with 60 km to go; he can also go with 15 km to go."The earlier an attack, the easier it will be to chase down for nations that have full squads, but it depends on who ends up in a breakaway."If Remco's not bridging to a powerhouse like a Mads Pedersen or Stefan Küng - a guy who's going to go pull-for-pull with him and just help carry him along in all the high-speed downhill and flat sections - if he goes up there with a bunch of people who are just swinging, not helping him, then maybe [he can be chased down]," says Creed."We hope the race gets chaotic, and we're able to go in some moves mid-late and not use a lot of energy - have the race come up there, and we have guys in both selections. Then we end up having numbers, and then we can play from there."It's such a delicate fine edge because you want to slip into moves rather than make the moves, and you want the people that you slip in with to be people who can carry a lot of the weight. You want some Mads Pedersen-type to go with Quinn - that's a good move. It's not necessarily a good move if Quinn and Del Toro go, because then it would be a better position to sit on, and Quinn's not going to want to sit on."Unlike in the past, Creed says riders from other countries aren't usually colluding because they share the same trade team the rest of the year."They don't do that anymore - they used to, but I think those days are gone. If you're on UAE, I think you're probably well-paid enough. That could probably happen if you had a guy who was like a straight-up domestique."You even saw last year in Kigali, Pogačar didn't wait for [Del Toro] - he kind of sat up for a second, and was like, 'Hey, you good?' And then was like, 'Oh, all right, well, I got to go, bye!' At the end of the day, they're there to win races, right?"If anything, maybe it would be like the social pressure - if you got into a two-up breakaway - of trying to pull just as hard as your teammate because you guys have a friendly rivalry. Like last year with Del Toro, maybe he should have sat on a little bit and been like, 'Bro, I'm wrecked,' but you know, you get excited and stuff. But no, that's not a problem. I mean, Quinn's teammates with Mads, you know, like, unfortunately everyone's got teammates."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. item.title: Today on Pinstripe Alley – 9/26/26
item.author: Andrew Mearns
item.content:encoded: A good chunk of the East Coast is getting slammed by a nor’easter this weekend, so if you’re in the area, we hope you stay safe! Since this current Yankees series against the Orioles is meaningless aside from the obvious goal of staying healthy, the game originally scheduled for today was played yesterday in a straight doubleheader. They’ll take a beat today and try to play tomorrow (rookie Elmer Rodríguez is announced as the probable starter for New York in a cameo), but if it doesn’t work out, it doesn’t work out. We may just have a 161-game regular season.Anyway, the postseason looms on Tuesday! Monday’s league-wide offday is the calm before the storm, but we’ll have plenty of material coming up then so consider today our personal Pinstripe Alley calm before the storm. It’s not all quiet though, as I’m on the Rivalry Roundup, Nick is celebrating the 101st (!) birthday of the oldest living Yankee, and Michael is discussing how the Yankees’ low-minors teams fared in 2026.Game preemptively moved up to yesterday for a twin bill, so it’s an offday with Game 162 tomorrow1. Assuming Carlos Rodón is not in the Wild Card Series rotation, what do you think is the best spot to potentially deploy him out of the bullpen?2. Think the Phillies continue their collapse and let the Diamondbacks steal the last NL Wild Card spot from them?

item.title: Yankees news: Schlittler, Fried still both in play to start Game 1
item.author: Jake Devin
item.content:encoded: MLB.com | Bryan Hoch: Cam Schlittler put the finishing touches on his Cy Young season Thursday night against the Rays. It wasn’t his sharpest start, Schlittler needing 70 pitches to navigate three innings, but it put his ERA on the season at 1.95, the lowest mark by a Yankee starter since Ron Guidry posted a 1.74 ERA in his legendary 1978 season, and the third-lowest ERA in franchise history. It’s also the lowest ERA by an American League starer since Justin Verlander’s 1.75 ERA in 2022, which won the future Hall of Famer* his third Cy Young.*Incidentally, Verlander is making his final career start today in Detroit.New York Post | Dan Martin: Speaking of Schlittler, you’d expect a pitcher of his stature to be a shoe-in for Game 1 of a playoff series. However, the Yankees are considering saving him for Game 2 of the AL Wild Card Series. Max Fried could start Game 1, on extra rest, and thus also give Schlittler an extra day of rest before the Yankees embark on what they hope will be a long postseason run. Schlittler would have enough rest to start Games 2 and 5 of a potential ALDS regardless of whether he pitches Game 1 or 2 of the Wild Card Series. Is it possible the Yankees are overthinking it? Yes, admits pitching coach Matt Blake, but these are precisely the things the club’s staff is paid to overthink.Whichever way the Yankees line things up, the good news is that their excellent rotation means that they’ll have an ace-caliber talent going every night. As an aside, Andrés wrote up this debate for earlier in the week, and that’s worth a read if you haven’t checked it out yet.The Athletic | Evan Drellich and Andrew Marchand: Drellich and Marchand report on the looming lockout, and one mark to look out for next year: 60 games. Apparently, if MLB misses 60 or more games in the 2027 season, the league’s national broadcast contracts would extend an extra year, into 2029. That introduces an interesting wrinkle into the owners’ calculus when it comes to this round of labor negotiations. On the one hand, the league would still receive their negotiated dues as part of their deals with their broadcast partners. On the other, extending those deals another year means the league can’t negotiate new national deals for another year; the league is likely seeking to earn a hefty raise on their next round of national contracts. The league also wouldn’t get paid in 2029 under this scenario. SNY | John Flanigan: Ryan Weathers threw a live bullpen session yesterday, facing hitters including Giancarlo Stanton and Trent Grisham. Aaron Boone said Weathers was up to 96 mph on his fastball, though called his control a little “scattered.” According to Boone, Weathers is on track to be an option during the playoffs, but it’s unclear if the Yankees will put the left-hander on the Wild Card roster. Carlos Lagrange also threw to hitters at Yankee Stadium yesterday, though it’s unlikely he’ll be on the playoff roster soon. Boone said he isn’t in play for the Wild Card roster and Matt Blake threw cold water on the idea of him debuting in the playoffs, though it still remains a (remote) possibility that Lagrange could factor into the Yankees’ plans later in the postseason if the team advances and Lagrange’s rehab continues to go well.

item.title: Yankees pitchers strike out a whopping 17 to split Orioles doubleheader
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: It wasn’t exactly a meaningful game, but the Yankees projected a much better image in the nightcap against the Baltimore Orioles and won it 6-3 after losing the first game in ugly fashion. New York’s pitchers certainly brought the strikeout stuff for this one, as Ryan Yarbrough, Will Warren, Brent Headrick, John Schreiber, and Alexander Cornielle combined to punch out 17 — tied for a team sign high among standard nine-inning efforts with a gem led by Cam Schlittler’s 13 on June 19th against the Reds.The Yankees’ record is now 93-68 with one regular season game left. If the weather holds off (no guarantees there), they have a shot at matching last year’s 94-68 record, which is frankly not bad because their best player, Aaron Judge, only suited up for 66 games. This game actually started as a pitchers’ duel, with Orioles’ starter Brandon Young and Yarbrough trading zeroes for the first 2.1 innings. The lefty departed after 49 pitches, but did not allow a run despite surrendering four hits and a walk, fanning five.The Yankees brought in Warren with one out and a runner on first, which represented a nice training scenario ahead of his expected bullpen role in the Wild Card Series.As it turned out, Warren was amazing, even though he allowed a double in that same inning that could have produced a run for Baltimore, and covered 3.2 scoreless frames while conceding a mere three hits and racking up seven strikeouts. He will finish the regular season with a nice 3.92 ERA and just over a strikeout per inning.The Yankees finally got to Young in the bottom of the fifth. After two outs, Austin Wells walked and crossed home thanks to Ryan McMahon’s RBI double.Young pitched a very solid game, completing five frames in which he conceded a single run on two hits and three walks. He whiffed six and finished the game and the season with a 3.56 ERA.The Bombers extended their lead in the bottom of the sixth against the O’s bullpen. Spencer Jones singled in Heliot Ramos, aided by a fielding error by right fielder Rece Hinds. Later in the inning, Anthony Volpe (playing shortstop with George Lombard Jr. getting a rare rest) hit an automatic double that plated Luis García Jr. and Jones to make it a 4-0 ballgame.Headrick replaced Warren in the seventh and surrendered the Orioles’ first run. With the bases loaded and one out, Leody Taveras hit a sac fly to bring in Pete Alonso. Ramos and García would hit consecutive RBI singles in the bottom of the inning, though, and the Yankees were up 6-1.Cornielle entered for his MLB debut, and was promptly greeted by a Dylan Beavers homer to right, making it a 6-2 ballgame. The rookie got into some trouble after the long ball, putting two men on base before getting the first out. He then surrendered a very long RBI double to Taveras that just missed the stands, as the O’s trimmed the Yankees lead to three runs.Cornielle then shook it off and struck out the next two hitters to end the ballgame on a high note. Ben Rice went 2-for-3 with a double, a walk, and a run scored, and McMahon went 2-for-4 with a double, a run, and an RBI. Volpe plated two, and Wells walked twice and scored once.The Yankees are supposed to wrap up their season on Sunday against the Orioles, starting at 3:20pm ET. Elmer Rodríguez has been announced as New York’s starter. However, the nor’easter that forced this doubleheader in the first place has led to some bad forecasts for Sunday, so it’s very possible that Game 162 gets nixed. We’ll find out soon enough! Stay dry out there.

item.title: Ashlin Barry’s Audacious U23 Worlds Win Proves the Power of Aero in Modern Cycling
item.author: Logan Jones-Wilkins
item.content:encoded: While Barry's win was massively impressive, his aero expertise and the new rules of hyper-fast road cycling show just how much cycling tactics continue to change.

item.title: New York Yankees vs. Baltimore Orioles: Ryan Yarbrough vs. Brandon Young
item.author: Andrés Chávez
item.content:encoded: After CC Sabathia’s No. 52 retirement ceremony and a rather forgettable Game 1 of Friday’s doubleheader, the New York Yankees will take the field again and face the Baltimore Orioles in the nightcap. The Bombers already know that they will host the Boston Red Sox in the Wild Card round, and the O’s are already eliminated from playoff contention.As a result, this is merely a tune-up game for New York, but that’s certainly not insignificant ahead of another edition of their rivalry with the Sox. Brandon Young will take the ball for Baltimore, trying to wrap up a solid year. The 28-year-old followed up his mediocre 57.2-inning cameo last year with a very solid campaign in 2026, with 151.2 frames of a 3.62 ERA, a 4.53 FIP, and 127 punchouts. He is not a star, but did more than enough to win a long-term spot on the O’s staff.The Yankees, with that series against their bitter rivals looming, didn’t announce their starting pitcher for Game 2 of the doubleheader until just about 10 minutes ago. Long reliever Ryan Yarbrough gets the nod for his second start of the season; he last pitched on Tuesday. His only other start of 2026 was the second game of another doubleheader against the Dodgers, when he went 2.2 shutout innings back on July 19th.Yarbrough is obviously not built up length-wise to go deep in this one either, but the expectation is that Will Warren will pitch a couple innings as preparation for the playoffs. He last pitched on Sunday in Arizona. Big things were expected from Warren this season, and while he didn’t exactly develop into an ace, he has been steady as a rock with a 4.02 ERA in 152.1 innings. A team would take that from its No. 5 starter any day of the week. David Bednar, Brent Headrick, and Paul Blackburn can only pitch so much, so Warren could certainly make a positive impact in the ‘pen.Also keep an eye on the bullpen for Alexander Cornielle. A career minor-league signed before the season, the right-hander made 16 starts for Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre and was activated to the big-league roster between games with matinee starter Brendan Beck optioned. If he appears tonight or Sunday, it will be his MLB debut.From this point forward, everything the Yankees do on the field will be with the Red Sox in mind, so don’t expect an all-out effort from those expected to be on the Wild Card Series roster. Indeed, there isn’t a ton of overlap between the Game 1 lineup and the Game 2 starting nine, as the Yankees are avoiding using too many players if possible. Indeed, the Game 1 infield went Paul Goldschmidt/José Caballero/George Lombard Jr./Anthony Volpe from first to third, and Game 2 has Luis García Jr./Jazz Chisholm Jr./Volpe/Ryan McMahon, with Volpe giving Lombard a spell by shifting over to his familiar six for the first time since his early-August demotion. Cody Bellinger tags in for Heliot Ramos in left, while Ramos shifts to right and Amed Rosario takes a seat. Austin Wells will catch and Spencer Jones is the only one starting the same position in both games, in center.: Yankee Stadium – Bronx, NY: 7:30 p.m. ET: WFAN 660/101.9 FM, WADO 1280 Gotham Sports App, MLB.tv (out-of-market only)

item.title: Yankees flop after CC Sabathia ceremony, lose to Orioles
item.author: Matt Ferenchick
item.content:encoded: With nothing left to play for on either side, the Yankees vs. Orioles series opener was somewhat overshadowed with the number retirement ceremony for CC Sabathia that took place before the game. The expected bad weather tomorrow forced a doubleheader today and moved the ceremony up to this afternoon as well. The short notice change led to the stands being emptier than anyone would like, but it was still a nice ceremony for the now-forever Yankees’ No. 52. Old friends Derek Jeter, Andy Pettitte, Dellin Betances, and Chris Young joined in the festivities on the field, alongside Sabathia’s family.On the field, things could’ve gone better.Making something of a spot start with the doubleheader and the Yankees planning ahead for the postseason, Brendan Beck started for the Yankees. Not that it was something the Yankees were considering, but Beck didn’t particularly make a case to be a last-second playoff roster addition. In his five innings, he allowed seven runs on six hits and three walks, including two home runs. The bullpen wasn’t particularly lights out following him, allowing the Orioles to build up a big lead.The Yankees’ offense was always going to be up against it considering that fact, but they didn’t do much. Orioles starter Trevor Rogers mostly kept the Yankees in check as Baltimore kept adding on. The Yankees could only plate one run from their eight hits, dooming them to a 10-2 loss in the first game of the doubleheader.On the mound, Beck started things off with a couple scoreless innings. However, Baltimore got on the board in the third. Beck nearly got through the inning again, but issued a two-out walk to Dylan Beavers. That came back to haunt him, as Pete Alonso did a Pete Alonso thing and homered to put the O’s in front.An inning later, Beck loaded the bases after walking two and allowing a single. Christian Franklin then dropped in a single, plating another Orioles’ run. After a force out got a runner at home, Beavers took Beck deep for a grand slam, putting Baltimore well in front.The Yankees got on the board themselves in the bottom of the fourth. Heliot Ramos reached with a triple, aided by center fielder Colton Cowser misplaying the carom off the wall. Amed Rosario followed that with an easy single to score the Yankees’ first run.Baltimore got that run back a short time later, thanks to an outfield miscue of the Yankees’ own. With reliever Yerry De los Santos in for the Yankees, Jeremiah Jackson hit a ball to deep right-center. The ball just got over the glove of Spencer Jones and took a fortuitous bounce past him. Jackson managed to race all the way around and beat the throw home for an inside-the-park homer, the first one in the Bronx in a dozen years — coincidentally with today’s honoree on the mound against Wil Myers. Alonso added a more conventional homer in the seventh in that it went over the fence, but it was unconventional in that it was an absolute bomb, 471 feet away.Honestly, I can’t even be mad at that one. Baltimore would tack on one more run to get to double digits for the game. Paul Blackburn and David Bednar got their work in as expected, and we now won’t see them again until the Wild Card Series.The Yankees did get one run back after Spencer Jones singled in the bottom of the ninth and eventually came around to score on a Paul Goldschmidt sacrifice fly. Ben Rice struck out looking to end it.One pretty disappointing thing to come out of the game was the play of the offense. Yes, the game didn’t actually mean anything, but the Yankees did send out the likes of Goldschmidt and Rosario and their theoretical “lefty” lineup. Them not doing much on offense isn’t what you would want to see considering that the Red Sox Wild Card Series lineup is now locked in and Boston has a bunch of left-handed pitchers they can throw at the Yankees.The second game of today’s doubleheader is set to begin at 7:30pm ET, which New York just announced. Brandon Young will go for Baltimore, while the Yankees will counter with Ryan Yarbrough, with Will Warren expected to provide relief work in anticipation of his playoff role.

item.title: UCI Road World Championships: Alejandra Neira takes junior women's road race title from five-rider escape in Montréal
item.author: jackie.tyson@futurenet.com (Jackie Tyson)
item.content:encoded: Alejandra Neira gave Spain their third gold medal of the UCI Road World Championships, winning the junior women's road race in a hotly-contested five-rider sprint in Montreal.Neira patiently waited until the final 150 metres to put in a massive turn of speed, leaving Matilde Rossignoli (Italy) in her wake to take silver, while Anja Grossmann (Switzerland) claimed third.After the dual titles from Benjamín Noval in the junior men's time trial and road race, Neira's gold medal represents the future of Spanish cycling."I can't believe it. It's the best day of my life," Neira said. "I can't believe that I'm the World Champion. It's incredible."Last year, it was Neira's teammate Paula Ostiz who won the title. Now it's her turn. "Paula is a big, big friend, also teammate, and to be the World Champion after her, wow, incredible."Neira was part of a three-rider escape along with Grossmann and Rossignoli, but the pair were caught in the final three kilometres by Maria Okrucińska (Poland) and Mirthe Mons (Netherlands), which shook her confidence a bit."When the other riders arrived, I lost a little bit my confidence, because Maria is a really good sprinter. But I tried to keep on her wheel, and then when I saw that I have to pass, I went."Grossmann finished fourth in the junior women's time trial, so found redemption with a bronze medal, though she said the final 26km were a challenge after a missed water bottle."I think the the last two laps were pretty intense and pretty tough because the Spanish girl attacked at the feed zone and I didn't catch my bottle there, so I rode like two laps without my bottle," she said at the post-race press conference. "That was hard because I got pretty bad cramps. But I think I worked really on my mental strength, and that just kept going. I'm not the best sprinter, but I just try to to sprint as best as I can."This year's route for the junior women measured 5.6km longer than the Kigali route and included a little more climbing, a total of 1,614 metres of elevation gain. Canada, Great Britain and Spain came with five riders each, giving them an edge with numbers.It was not until the second lap that the complexion of the peloton began to change, with riders falling off the back rather than anyone accelerating away. Spain, Australia and Poland were represented at the front.With just under 45km to go, French rider Sidonie Vachet put a spark in the proceedings with an attack at the front of a fractured peloton. She opened a slight 16-second gap on the uphill to start a fourth circuit, marking the halfway point of the 80.4km race.Behind, Scout Wellmeier (USA) rode at the front with Lluna Jimenez (Spain), Eva Drhova (Czechia), the Australian duo Chloe Bowen and Neve Parslow, and Polish duo Maria Okrucińska and Amelia Szymańska, and another 31 riders packed into the peloton.Bright sunshine helped the temperatures rise as high as 24°C (76°F), the warmest afternoon of the championships so far, and riders took on plenty of liquids at the feed zone along the climb. Across the summit of the Camillien-Houde, Vachet relented to the pace behind and the race reset.Once across the Polytechnique climb and on the twisting city-centre streets of Montréal, Great Britain riders could be seen gathering at the front. But it was an acceleration from Colombia's Zara Sofia Lamprea that came on the approach to the Parc Avenue climb.Lamprea carried a 10-second advantage, with Wellmeier trailing in solo second. The reduced peloton of 35 riders began the chase with two laps remaining at 20 seconds.There was a crash at the front of the race under a heavy canopy of trees, with Lamprea and Wellmeier going down. Both were back riding quickly, but as they made the penultimate ascent of Camillien-Houde, the chase began closing down their effort.A group of 10 crested the summit, and Lamprea just a few seconds behind and Wellmeier farther back, now chasers. France, Spain and Germany each had two riders, with one rider each from the USA, Netherlands, Great Britain and Switzerland. Then on the back side of Mont Royal, more riders tagged along for a bigger group.Riders upped the pace to position at the front, passing crowds at the Polytechnique Montréal centre for science and technology, with a series of twisting turns on the descent causing riders to go wide on the course.With 18.5km to go, Nabyenka García (Mexico) was the next rider to put in an extra effort, gapping the field by 15 seconds quickly on a flatter section. The Mexican rider looked back several times, and finally kept on the accelerator to go alone.The bell lap rang with long shadows forming in the late Canadian afternoon, García still out front but only by 14 seconds. The curse of race leaders continued as she stopped for a mechanical, looking to reposition her chain, and was forced back in the peloton.Wellmeier, Vachet, Parslow, Orucińska and Lidia Castro (Spain) were setting the pace at the bottom of the final ascent. Mirthe Mons (Netherlands) pushed the pace at the front, which seemed to spur others to give it a go. Soon a trio were at the front - Anja Grossmann (Switzerland), Alejandra Neira (Spain) and Matilde Rossignoli (Italy) - and with 10km to go had 20 seconds on Okrucińska and Mons.With 4km to go, the trio weren't showing signs of working togehter, which allowed Mons and Okrucińska, the new world time trial champion, to edge closer in the chase. "Maybe we should have worked a little bit more together, so the other two wouldn't came back. But that's junior racing because junior racing is always a little bit more hectic and a little bit more without a clear tactic. I wanted to work together, but it was not my decision," Grossmann said later.With 2km to go, there were five to fight for three medals.Mons struck first on the final climb. Then mountain bike world champion Grossman passed, then Rossignoli, but it was Neira who went wide on the right side and took the victory.Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia. Subscribers get unlimited access to exclusive analysis from our expert columnists, in-depth features and industry-leading tech insight. Plus, the Cyclingnews app lets you follow the action wherever you go! item.title: How to watch Yankees vs. Red Sox in AL Wild Card Series: Start times, channels, and more
item.author: Dani Mohr
item.content:encoded: The MLB postseason is finally upon us, and the No. 4 seed Yankees are kicking things off by facing the Red Sox in the Wild Card Series, just as they did in 2025. New York will end the season at least four games better than Boston, but as they say, all records reset to 0-0 come October — or very-late September in the case of the 2026 season.The Red Sox defeated the Cubs on Friday afternoon to officially clinch the No. 5 seed, meaning the Yankees will have home-field advantage by starting the postseason in the Bronx. They already knew they would be hosting, but it wasn’t yet official that they would face Boston. Per MLB’s Sarah Langs, this will be the seventh all-time postseason meeting between the Yanks and Red Sox, tied for the second-most common matchup in league history and trailing only the 12 famous Yankees/Dodgers World Series rumbles. New York and Boston have each won three series apiece in the playoff head-to-heads.You won’t want to miss all the action in the best-of-three series next week, with the winner advancing to face the Rays in the American League Division Series in a race for the pennant.Here’s all the information you’ll need to know to tune into every game this weekend. This post will be updated with first pitch times as soon as they are announced, though given the hubbub that usually surrounds Yankees/Red Sox, it would be a surprise if they weren’t all night games.How to watch Yankees vs. Red Sox in Wild Card Series Tuesday, September 29 TBD: NBCPeacock Wednesday, September 30 TBD: NBCPeacock Thursday, October 1 TBD: NBCPeacock

item.title: 'We gave it everything' - Aubin Sparfel ready to join Paul Seixas at Decathlon CMA CGM after Montreal Worlds disappointment
item.author: kirsten.frattini@futurenet.com (Kirsten Frattini)
item.content:encoded: Rising talent Aubin Sparfel ends his under-23 career in disappointment, having finished just off the podium in fourth place in the under-23 men's race at the UCI Road World Championships on Friday.The 20-year-old French rider came into the race as the big favourite, and was hoping to secure the rainbow jersey. Now, he will turn his attention to joining compatriot Paul Seixas in the WorldTour with Decathlon CMA CGM after spending four seasons growing through the team's development ranks. "We are a little bit disappointed, but we gave it everything," Sparfel told "Of course, we were here for the victory. It's like that. I'm super proud of the team and proud of myself. I had a super amount of pressure on me after the win last week [Grand Prix de Wallonie], and I felt like I could finally dream about winning."Sparfel had another successful season with the Decathlon CMA CGM Development programme, kicking off the year with an overall victory at Le Tour de Bretagne Cycliste, taking sixth overall at Boucles de la Mayenne-Crédit Mutuel, fourth overall at Giro d'Italia Next Gen, and winning a stage of the Tour de l'Avenir. He capped off his season with a victory at the one-day Lotto Grand Prix de Wallonie, showing top form heading into these Worlds and setting himself up as one of the favourites."Of course, I learned a lot this year. I won a lot, and I think I'm ready to step up. It was a super good season, and I can thank everyone around me. My team, the France team, my coaches and my family. It was a super good year," he said.During the under-23 men's road race, Sparfel joined a chase group that also included silver medallist Héctor Álvarez (Spain) and bronze medallist Jesper Stiansen (Norway) in a failed effort to bring back new world champion Ashlin Barry (USA).Despite his disappointment in finishing fourth, Sparfel praised Barry on his winning performance. "Ashlin was super strong," Sparfel told . "We knew that he could win this year, but we did everything we could as a team, and we were super strong as a team. "In the last two laps we did a lot with the other guys from the big favourites, but in the end, we arrived in the race for second place - it's like that."Sparfel will now turn his attention to racing alongside Seixas, fourth overall in the Tour de France this year and a favourite in the elite men's road race on Sunday. The two riders are among the nation's most promising talents on the WorldTour."I will go to the WorldTour, so I will no longer race in the under-23s. I've ridden on every team with Paul since we were juniors and know him really well," Sparfel told ."I will race for Decathlon next season, and we will see what we can do. I will speak with the team about my race program, but I'm proud of my under-23 racing season, and now I will focus on elite for next season."Subscribe to Cyclingnews for comprehensive race coverage of both the UCI Road and Gravel World Championships, alongside the final monument of the season, Il Lombardia.
